name: clipping
title: Stripes clipped to shapes
summary: The same diagonal stripe pattern clipped three ways: to a square with clipRect, to a circle path and to a star path with clipPath.
prompt: Fill a square, a circle and a star with the same diagonal stripe pattern by clipping it to each shape.
teaches: Restrict drawing to a rectangle with clipRect inside a save block
Mask a pattern with any path id via clipPath (a pathExpression circle, a pathCreate star)
Scope each clip with save {commands} so it ends when the block restores
Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre
pitfalls: A clip only shrinks: without the surrounding save block the second clip intersects the first and nothing is drawn
Clip paths are only used, never drawn: create them before the clipPath, and draw an outline separately if one is wanted
Make the pattern overshoot the clip on every side; the stripes start 100 dp left of the square so the bottom-left corner is covered
Draw the labels outside the save blocks, or they are clipped away too

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: literal coordinates sit in the top-left and get cut off when it is resized, so scale the drawing to fit (or derive positions from componentWidth()/componentHeight())

snippets.note: save { clipRect, stripes }: the clip ends with the block
a closed circle path: pathExpression of cos/sin with flags 1 (loop)
pathCreate starts the star path; pathAppendLineTo adds its vertices
15 diagonal stripes from the loop index

check.describe: Blue stripes fill only a square, teal only a disc, yellow only a star; nothing outside. Resized, the whole drawing scales uniformly to fit and stays centred (smaller in a narrow box, centred with margins in a wide one).
